newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak SAX falls, blue chips mixed.
newsitem.headline: Slovak SAX falls, blue chips mixed.

text.p: Slovak blue chips closed mixed, pulling the SAX index slightly down in moderate trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Friday, with brokers expecting livelier trading in the near future.
"Though traded volumes were mostly not interesting on Friday, there were already signs of revival on the market," Bohus Betko of ING Barings said.
He added he expected increased investor interest in the near future due to the current downtrend on the neighbouring Czech market.
Steel maker VSZ dominated trading on the BSE floor, with 1,015 traded shares, closing up nine crowns at 750 crowns. Last week the company said it had proposed a 40-crown dividend on 1996 profits.
"What we see (in VSZ) is certainly a result of a dividend announcement," Betko said.
He added he expected VSZ to rise until the company's annual shareholders meeting, scheduled for May 21.
Oil refiner Slovnaft, which is the most capitalised Bratislava issue, closed unchanged at 1,015, but Betko said there were the signs of weakness in the share.
"It seems that demand for this share has been already fulfilled and I think it will decrease to some 1,000 crowns," he added.
Overall volume increased to 726,061 shares, from 147,747 shares traded on Wednesday, while turnover jumped to 683.1 million crowns, from 75.16 million.
